category: Migration playbooks (vendor displacement + remote-access plays + methodology)

notes.catalogue: The catalogue PNGs at scratchpad/catalogue/*.png render as solid black shapes (CSS fills missing), so figure content was checked against the README figure list and the FIGS label text in _extract/diagram-kit/kit-host.html. No source figure tells a co-existence story with an incumbent (parallel Socket + legacy edge + handoff, or two steering planes), which is what every page in this category draws, so every page is {draw:true}; each diagram carries a figConsidered note naming the figures weighed and why they were rejected.
notes.slots: Every page has one diagram-card -> slot 'main'. migration-methodology has two cards: the hub-interconnect topology (inside section#solution, slot 'main') and the Option F regional-eBGP diagram (slot 'card-2').
notes.viewbox: vb is '0 0 760 560' (kit default, matching the other categories). Briefs are positional (LEFT/CENTRE/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM) so they re-flow; current page SVGs are 960 wide, and '0 0 960 540' is an acceptable fallback if the auto-fit warns on labels. Node counts are <=11 per diagram.
notes.logos: No vendor logos in the kit. Incumbents are named in node text only (FortiGate, Viptela, ZIA, PA firewall, Quantum gateway, XGS, ASA 5500-X, NSa/TZ, ProxySG/WSS, iboss, Netskope NewEdge, Cloudflare Zero Trust, VOS, EC appliance, Forcepoint cloud, DirectAccess gateway, ASA/FTD headend).
notes.legend_kinds: Legend kinds use the fl-* line classes without the prefix: tun, ipsec, priv, https, flow, ha, net, hot, dim, down, attack, plus 'live'. Interim/legacy paths are drawn with fl-ha (amber) and retired/blocked paths with fl-down (red) to match the current pages' amber/red convention.
notes.convention: In every brief: GREEN = Cato tunnel (fl-tun) or brokered flow (fl-flow); AMBER = interim/legacy path (fl-ha); RED = retired/blocked (fl-down) or attack (fl-attack); DASHED GREY = rollback lever (fl-dim, np:0, arrow).
notes.shape: Per page: {spotlight, diagram, title, desc, legend, keepCaption, carry}. 'diagram' is the main card. migration-methodology additionally carries 'diagrams' (main + card-2 Option F) with per-card title/desc/legend, and picSlot 'main'. Each diagram has 'brief' (prose drawing instructions), plus structured 'nodes' ([title<=22ch, sub, cls, icon]) and 'flows' ([path, fl-class (+ decorations), label]) that the brief must agree with.
notes.spotlight: All flow ids, marker anchors and hl components validated against the README tables; every step <=110 chars; 3-6 hl components per page.
notes.journeys: No journey pages in this set (migration-journey-* are excluded by the id regex and belong to migration-policy-journeys.json).

steps.t: Discovery first: where does the routing decision between legacy and Cato live at each site?
An interconnect hub holds legacy CPE and a Cato Socket; an L3 switch or firewall routes between them.
Migrated sites reach legacy sites over the Cato backbone and the hub; sites move in waves.
Rollback is a route change: re-add the routed range or withdraw the BGP prefix, no site visit.

steps.t: Sockets and the Cato Client take transport and WAN security first; ZCC stays on the endpoint.
During transition the PoP backhauls internet traffic to ZIA over parallel IKEv2 IPsec tunnels.
Converted internet policy is proven on a test cohort, then flipped to direct PoP breakout.

LEFT column (edges): nd 'Branch site | Cato Socket X1500 · WAN + internet via PoP' (icon building, sub-line 2 may be 'WAN + internet via PoP'); below it nd 'Remote user | Cato Client + ZCC' (icon laptop) with a small pill m 'ZCC rides inside Cato tunnel'. CENTRE: popBox 'Cato PoP | SWG · CASB/DLP · TLSi' sitting on a ring() 'Global Private Backbone'. RIGHT: cloud 'Internet & SaaS | M365 · web · cloud apps' top-right; nd cls:'dash' 'Zscaler ZIA | interim · being retired' (icon globe, pill y 'interim') bottom-right. FLOWS: fl-tun (green, animated) Branch -> PoP and Remote user -> PoP. fl-ha (amber, animated, label 'IKEv2 IPsec · LB by src / dst') PoP -> Zscaler ZIA, then fl-ha np:0 arrow ZIA -> Internet (legacy egress). fl-flow (green, arrow, label 'direct breakout — target') PoP -> Internet & SaaS. 6 nodes + cloud. Keep the amber path visibly temporary (dashed) and the green direct path solid.

migration-zscaler.title: Phased co-existence of Cato and Zscaler ZIA during migration
migration-zscaler.desc: Sites and users connect to the nearest Cato PoP; internet traffic is tunnelled on to ZIA over parallel IKEv2 IPsec while policies are converted, then flipped to direct breakout from the Cato PoP — no big-bang cutover.
carry: Branch site uses Cato Socket X1500; remote user runs Cato Client + ZCC with the ZCC tunnel riding inside the Cato tunnel
PoP stack label: SWG · CASB/DLP · TLSi; backbone labelled Global Private Backbone
Interim path label exactly: 'IKEv2 IPsec · LB by src / dst'; target path 'direct breakout — target'; ZIA marked 'interim · being retired'
Internet & SaaS examples: M365 · web · cloud apps

Prose: interim ZIA tunnels egress from the Cato PoP nearest Zscaler over the Tier-1 backbone; deck example 3 active + 3 backup tunnels; up to six active tunnels per HA role; two other interim patterns (site FW → ZIA; FW/Cato VLAN termination) keep breakout on existing kit

steps.t: The Socket installs in parallel; the PA firewall stays default gateway while subnets hand off per prefix.
Migrated subnets reach the internet and other Cato sites through the PoP; the rest keeps its PA route.
GlobalProtect cohorts move to the Cato Client wave by wave; rollback is a route withdrawal.

migration-palo-alto.title: Phased co-existence of a Palo Alto firewall and a Cato Socket during migration
migration-palo-alto.desc: The PA firewall stays default gateway while a parallel Socket takes migrated subnets per prefix over an eBGP or static handoff on a LAN transit VLAN; an interconnect hub keeps the legacy and Cato islands talking and GlobalProtect cohorts move to the Cato Client in waves.
legend: Legacy path via the PA — interim, retired at cutover
carry: PA firewall (HA) is 'default gateway — today'; Cato Socket X1500 'installed in parallel'; handoff is 'eBGP / static handoff over LAN transit VLAN'
PoP stack: FWaaS · IPS · TLSi · SWG; Legacy WAN: MPLS · Internet · GP VPN; Interconnect hub = Socket + legacy CPE bridging Cato ↔ legacy
Two user cohorts: GlobalProtect cohort (GP VPN → PA gateway, being retired in waves) and Cato Client cohort (SDP · target state); 'users migrate in waves →'
Flow labels 'default route' (legacy) and 'migrated subnets' (Cato); prose: community 32768 isolation, no zone construct, dual VPN clients not recommended
Prose dates not on the diagram: PA-3200/5200 support ends 31 Aug 2028 (EOS Aug 2023); CVE-2024-3400 CVSS 10.0; Expedition EOL 31 Dec 2024; TLSi not supported on Android

steps.t: Each cohort swaps the Netskope Client for the Cato Client in one window — never both tunnels at once.
Sites run the legacy IPsec/GRE tunnel and a Cato Socket side by side, split per VLAN.
Private apps go on-net behind a Socket, replacing NPA Publishers; API Data Protection retires last.

migration-netskope.desc: Each wave uninstalls the Netskope Client and installs the Cato Client in one window; the site runs parallel paths per VLAN, and private apps move from NPA Publishers to routed reachability behind a Socket while the Publisher stays dormant as the rollback.

steps.t: Regional Cato hubs peer over eBGP with each Viptela hub (or the L3 core behind a Meraki MX), keeping symmetry.
A migrated spoke rides the Cato backbone with DNS and web security enforced at the PoP — Umbrella bypassed.
AnyConnect cohorts swap to the Cato Client; disabling a spoke withdraws its routes, re-enabling it rolls back.

migration-cisco.desc: The migrated spoke rides the Cato backbone with DNS and web security enforced at the PoP; the legacy spoke stays on the Viptela overlay and Umbrella, and eBGP at the regional interconnect with OMP-to-BGP redistribution keeps routing symmetric so spoke cutover withdraws routes automatically.

steps.t: A parallel Socket at each FortiGate regional hub exchanges routes with the hub over an eBGP handoff.
Cross-region routes carry an extra AS hop, so best-path keeps every flow symmetric via its local hub.
Disable the FortiGate spoke, bring up the Cato site, routes propagate; rollback is re-enabling the spoke.

carry: Hub site is 'Regional hub site — parallel deployment' with 'Cato Socket | parallel at the hub' and 'FortiGate hub | SD-WAN / ADVPN core'; eBGP label 'AS-path anchors symmetry'

steps.t: Cohort A keeps its GPO-pushed PAC and steers explicitly to the policy-frozen Forcepoint cloud.
Cohort B steers transparently — Cato Client with Always-On, sites via Socket — to the nearest PoP.
One TLS inspection owner per cohort; the Forcepoint DLP endpoint agent stays for USB, print and clipboard.

TOP LANE (amber, interim): nd cls:'dash' 'Cohort A — on PAC | Explicit proxy via GPO · browser → PAC → proxy' (icon users, pill y) -> fl-ha animated labelled 'PAC via GPO — explicit' -> nd cls:'dash' 'Forcepoint cloud | policy-frozen · interim' (icon globe, pill y 'web policy still here') -> fl-ha arrow -> shared cloud at far right 'Internet & SaaS | M365 · web · SaaS apps'. BOTTOM LANE (green, target): nd 'Cohort B — migrated | Cato Client · Always-On · sites steer via Socket' (icon users, pill g) -> fl-tun animated labelled 'transparent — no PAC' -> popBox 'Cato PoP | SWG · TLSi · CASB · DLP' sitting on a short ring() 'Global Private Backbone' -> fl-flow arrow labelled 'direct PoP breakout' -> the same Internet & SaaS cloud. NOTE NODE bottom-left under Cohort B: side() 'DLP hybrid | FP endpoint agent stays · USB · print · clipboard' (icon shield). 5 nodes + 1 cloud. The two lanes never cross.

migration-forcepoint.title: Dual steering planes during the Forcepoint-to-Cato transition
migration-forcepoint.desc: Cohort A's PAC still sends web traffic explicitly to the policy-frozen Forcepoint cloud while cohort B steers transparently through the Cato Client and Sockets to the Cato PoP; exactly one platform owns TLS inspection per cohort and the Forcepoint DLP endpoint agent stays for its exclusive channels.
carry: Cohort A — on PAC: explicit proxy via GPO, 'browser → PAC → proxy'; Forcepoint cloud 'policy-frozen · interim', 'web policy still here'
Cohort B — migrated: Cato Client · Always-On, 'sites steer via Socket'; labels 'transparent — no PAC' and 'direct PoP breakout'

steps.t: The Cato Client connects to the nearest PoP with SSO and MFA at the IdP — no concentrator to find.
Device posture is checked continuously at the PoP, and access is to named apps, not a subnet.
